title.narrative: Parana Public Sector Modernization and Innovation for Service Delivery Operation

description.narrative: The Program development objectives are to respond to the COVID-19 pandemic and improve the efficiency of health and other priority public services.

The Program supports the State government's efforts to improve public administration institutions, aiming to deliver better public services and enhance the social and economic impacts of the government's COVID-19 recovery plan. It builds on lessons learned from a previous SWAp operation, the Parana Multi-sector Development Project (P126343), and focuses on strengthening institutions for evidence-based public service delivery as well as improving planning and public investment management (PIM).The Program, designed as a hybrid operation, is structured around two interlinked components. The first component, financed by a Program for Results (PforR) loan, supports initiatives in health services (Results Area 1), environmental and disaster risk management information systems (Results Area 2), and regional development planning and PIM (Results Area 3). Its objective is to enhance public administration and service delivery, with a particular focus on pandemic mitigation and recovery. The PforR supports five Borrower programs and budget lines in the Pluriannual Plan (PPA) 2020-2023 and the Annual Budget Law (LOA), including programs that have been carried over to the new PPA (2024-2027).The second component, financed by an Investment Project Financing (IPF) loan, provides technical assistance and capacity-building support to strengthen the institutional capacity of various departments within the State of Parana government. It supports the development and implementation of a new integrated PIM system, including the creation of new methodologies and manuals for investment management. Human Resources Management (HRM) support includes strategic workforce planning, training programs, and a review of the civil servant health insurance program. Digital innovation in the state is promoted through the development of a new platform to enhance public policy solutions and support Parana's innovation strategy. Finally, implementation support—including coverage of Project Management Unit (PMU) operational costs, internal controls and verification of Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs), as well as change management and capacity-building activities—is also part of the IPF.The Level 2 restructuring addressed the State's revised priorities by introducing changes to activities and indicators, including new DLIs, primarily to strengthen health service delivery. Specifically, in Results Area 1, the focus shifts from converting Small Hospitals into Multiprofessional Care Units to implementing Cardiovascular Care Guidelines to address chronic cardiovascular diseases (CVD), following evidence-based recommendations for the prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and management of CVD. Additionally, digital strategies will improve health service coordination, including technological solutions for the state referral and counter-referral information system and an ambulance management system. Other changes include refining activities and indicators in other areas, adjusting disbursement arrangements and estimates, and extending the closing date by six months.

condition.narrative: For purposes of carrying out Part 1 (a) of the Program, the Borrower, through the State of Health Secretariat (SESA), shall enterinto an agreement with each of the Participating Municipalities (the “Commitment Agreement”), under terms and conditions acceptableto the Bank, including the obligation to: (i) carry out the activities which fall within their administrative jurisdiction underthe Program; and (ii) comply with the pertinent provisions of the Legal Agreement, including complying with the provisions of theOperational Manual and the Anti-Corruption Guidelines.

No later than forty-five (45) days after the Effective Date, the Borrower shall establish, and thereafter, operate and maintain,throughout the implementation of the Operation, a Steering Committee (the “Steering Committee”), responsible for Operationoversight and coordination, with the composition, functions and resources set forth in the Operational Manual.

The Borrower shall establish, and thereafter operate and maintain, at all times during the execution of the Operation, a ProgramManagement Unit (PMU) within the State Secretariat of Planning and Structured Projects (SEPL) to implement, coordinate, monitor andreport on the execution of the Operation, with qualifications, functions, key staff, capacity and resources, all satisfactory tothe Bank, as further detailed in the Operational Manual.
The Borrower shall furnish to the Bank each Program Report and Project Report not later than ninety (90) days after the end of eachcalendar semester, covering the calendar semester.
The Borrower, through SEPL, shall ensure that the Project is implemented in accordance with the Environmental and Social CommitmentPlan (“ESCP”), in a manner acceptable to the Bank.
The Borrower, through SEPL, shall undertake the actions set forth in the Program Action Plan in a manner satisfactory to the Bank.

The SEPL shall appoint and thereafter maintain, at all times during the implementation of the Program, an independent verificationagency with terms of reference (ToR) acceptable to the Bank (“Independent Verification Agency”), to verify the data and otherevidence supporting the achievement of one or more Disbursement-Linked Results (DLR).
